menu.title: The tea-maker and the slowly returning fan
menu.concept: In a hot Renaissance-inspired tea workroom, a maker handwinds a spring-powered brass table fan; a visible gear train drives an eccentric crank and connecting rod, returning a folded silk fan toward her flushed face while her other hand steadies the base. The care is a small practical relief during work.

menu.title: The bookbinder saves a broken spine
menu.concept: A bookbinder in a lamplit Renaissance workshop uses a weight-driven small press; a descending suspended weight and rope drum turn exposed reduction gears that close two wooden padded jaws gently around the repaired book. Her fingertips guide the loose spine into alignment.

menu.title: The last clean length of linen
menu.concept: A laundress in a Renaissance washhouse feeds a damp linen strip into a weight-driven tabletop mangle. A suspended stone weight, rope drum and visible gears rotate two wooden rollers; she smooths an emerging clean fold beside a worn fabric basket.

menu.title: The seedling keeper resets the water clock
menu.concept: A courtyard herb gardener winds a spring-driven brass irrigation regulator. An exposed spring barrel and meshing gears turn a lobed cam that presses a small valve lever; one fine stream lands in a seedling tray while she shields the fragile leaves with an open hand.
